question: Does one causal three-pair confirmation layer reduce local-flow-driven below-reference triggers while retaining the frozen positive-window response?
non_goals: changing rotation compensation, Sparse LK, local affine fitting, or support-manager behavior
confirmation, Android, product, or safety authority

data_partitions.identity_basis: Immutable 967-pair A4 ledger already used for development and the validated R0 attribution result.

single_revision.confirmation_rule: revised_trigger is true only when the current pair and the two immediately preceding pairs in the same window are evaluable and each exceeds 0.01/s
single_revision.reset_rule: Any abstention, window boundary, or pair at or below threshold resets the consecutive-pair count to zero.

constraints.description: Old and revised ledgers contain the same ordered 967 pair identities, roles, timestamps, evaluability, and continuous compensated-expansion values.
Exactly one fixed confirmation rule is evaluated; no alternative length, majority rule, threshold, or estimator is computed.
The median fixed-denominator below-reference trigger coverage is reduced by at least 30 percent relative to old.
constraints.rationale: A development revision should materially affect the diagnosed 34.78 percent false-trigger burden rather than produce a cosmetic change.
constraints.calibration_source: The old frozen below-reference aggregate and the R0 attribution showing short local-flow bursts.
constraints.sensitivity_plan: No neighboring confirmation length is run on these development windows; any sensitivity study requires a new version or new external data.
constraints.revision_policy: Fixed for R1 and never changed after R1 outcome access.

constraints.description: The revised positive role aggregate retains at least 90 percent of old fixed-denominator trigger coverage.
constraints.rationale: The targeted false-trigger fix must preserve the already supported positive direction.
constraints.calibration_source: The old frozen positive aggregate; 90 percent limits the loss to a small temporal-onset cost.
constraints.sensitivity_plan: Report both positive windows separately; do not tune the rule if one misses.
constraints.revision_policy: Fixed for R1 and never changed after R1 outcome access.

constraints.description: Each positive window adds no more than 0.25 seconds from the old first trigger to the revised first trigger.
constraints.rationale: Three consecutive pairs imply about 0.07 seconds at ETH3D cadence and 0.20 seconds at TartanAir 10 Hz; 0.25 seconds is the deterministic cadence-bound allowance.
constraints.calibration_source: Frozen source-native pair timestamps, not outcome optimization.
constraints.sensitivity_plan: Report exact per-window delay and do not test a second temporal length.
constraints.revision_policy: Fixed for R1 and never changed after R1 outcome access.

constraints.description: Revised positive aggregate trigger coverage remains strictly greater than revised below-reference coverage.
constraints.rationale: The revision cannot invert the only direction supported by A4.
constraints.sensitivity_plan: Report both role aggregates and all four windows; no pooled-only rescue.
constraints.revision_policy: Fixed for R1 and never changed after R1 outcome access.

successor_policy.pass_successor: Decide whether the single revised implementation merits a separately frozen external confirmation dataset.
successor_policy.fail_successor: Stop this revision on the frozen development cohort; do not test another revision automatically.

experiment_design.minimal_discriminating_experiment: Apply one causal three-pair confirmation rule to the immutable 967-pair ledger and compare old versus revised outcomes on all four frozen windows.
experiment_design.resource_budget: One deterministic ledger pass, one independent aggregate replay, no RGB decode, no network, and no additional candidate.
experiment_design.stop_conditions: Stop after the R1 result and validator; PASS permits only an external-validation decision, while any gate miss closes this implementation version.
experiment_design.efficiency_strategy: Reuse the exact continuous pair outputs because the revision changes only causal trigger confirmation.

hypotheses.theoretical_or_empirical_basis: R0 attribution assigns 160 of 198 geometry-below old triggers to baseline local-flow threshold crossings, while below trigger runs last at most eight pairs and positive runs are sustained.
hypotheses.causal_difference: Adds only a causal persistence requirement after the unchanged pair estimator.
hypotheses.expected_information_gain: Tests whether short local-flow excursions, rather than the continuous expansion direction, explain the development false-trigger burden.
hypotheses.minimal_test: One old-versus-revised replay over the same ordered 967 pairs.
hypotheses.evaluation_metric: Below relative trigger reduction, positive trigger retention, positive onset delay, and role direction.
hypotheses.resource_budget: One deterministic CPU pass over 967 JSONL rows.
hypotheses.stop_condition: Do not alter or replace the candidate after reading its result.
hypotheses.selection_reason: It directly targets the dominant diagnosed mechanism without changing data, thresholds, compensation, flow, affine fitting, or support recovery.

failure_learning.observation: The single R1 candidate has not been evaluated.
alternative_explanations: positive and below windows may share similar short-run structure
three-pair confirmation may reduce positive coverage too much
pairwise expansion may require a different estimator in a future version
reuse_candidates: R1 can remain a deterministic regression fixture even if not ready.
